extracted.intended_audience: readers, editors, and critics of travel literature and literary biography; historians assessing the reliability and merits of travel narratives
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for judging travel books and biographies (focusing on authenticity, factual importance, style, authorship, and treatment of contentious topics). Useful for critics, editors, and historians assessing the quality and trustworthiness of a traveller's account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic and important information
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential merit of this book consists in the authentic and important information which it contains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to factual authenticity and the significance of discoveries (e.g., new geographical facts). Literary beauty is secondary to the value of accurate, important information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness of description
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearness of the descriptions, the natural and easy flow of the narration, and the general elegance of the style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether places, events, and people are described with clarity and whether the narrative progresses naturally. Look for readable prose that aids comprehension rather than ornamental flourishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firsthand eyewitness testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts ascertained by the unexceptionable testimony of an eye-witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to claims established by direct observation. Eye‑witness testimony can convert reasonable conjectures into established facts (illustrated by Park's confirmation of the Niger's course).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and importance of discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: The work may be regarded as the greatest accession to the general stock of geographical knowledge made by any single traveller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the magnitude and novelty of contributions to knowledge (e.g., correcting prevailing geographic theories). Important, novel findings substantially increase a work's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of physical and social detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains many interesting details concerning the face of the country, its soil and productions, the condition of the inhabitants; their principal occupations, manners and habits of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge thoroughness across physical geography, natural history, economy and social customs. Rich, varied details that illuminate both environment and people strengthen the narrative's utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral geography / cultural observation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations concerning the kind and amiable dispositions of the Negro inhabitants, contrasted with the intolerance and brutality of the Moors; existence of populous cities and higher state of improvement inland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the sensitivity, accuracy, and depth of cultural and moral observations. Prefer balanced, context-aware accounts over hasty generalizations or stereotyped portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of hardships and character under duress
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulties and dangers endured by the author and the rare union of prudence, temper and perseverance with ardour and enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether descriptions of suffering, danger, and personal conduct feel credible and are recounted with appropriate restraint and insight (not sensationalized). Such portrayals add value when they convey truth convincingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and unaffected manner
rubrics_metrics.description: His natural and unaffected manner of describing exertions and sufferings carries a feeling and conviction of truth to the mind of every reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer an unaffected style that inspires conviction; beware of overwrought or obviously manufactured emotionalism which undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment (or omission) of contentious/political issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Silence on a controversial subject (e.g., the Slave Trade) may itself be evidence of bias; an author's abstention from explicit opinion can function as a de facto declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize whether the author addresses major contemporary controversies adequately. Omission or cursory treatment of known causes/context can indicate bias or undue influence; explicit neutrality warrants examination for its practical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and transparency of external assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of another person's assistance in composition (e.g., Mr. Bryan Edwards revised and corrected the manuscript; whole of his narrative was incorporated by permission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether editorial or compositorial help is acknowledged and whether the compiler made correct and proper use of materials. Assistance is acceptable when transparently handled and when it does not compromise authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity and consistency of style
rubrics_metrics.description: No inequalities are apparent in Park's narrative; passages inserted from another's memoir are not distinguishable; the style is throughout uniform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stylistic coherence across the work—abrupt stylistic shifts or visible mash-ups of voices detract from unity. Uniform style suggests careful revision or skilled compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of literary ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally pleasing, but perhaps too much laboured in places; tendency to ambitious ornament is conspicuous in some parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether ornamentation serves the subject or distracts. Excessive ambition in style can undermine simplicity and authenticity; simplicity is often preferable for travel narrative truth-telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration by internal evidence and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The authenticity of the work is apparent from the internal evidence of many parts of the narrative, and from the known character of Park and Mr. Edwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for internal consistency, specific verifiable details, and external corroboration (character, other sources, appendices) to support trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and preservation of source materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials consisted of short notes or memoranda forming an imperfect journal; where these were wanting he supplied the deficiency from memory; many loose papers were mislaid or destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the documentary basis: presence of contemporaneous notes/journals strengthens reliability; reconstruction from memory or lost primary papers weakens evidentiary value and calls for caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of expert appendices and geographical illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: An important Memoir by Major Rennell consisting of geographical illustrations formed a valuable appendage to the edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the presence of specialist appendices, maps, or expert commentary which substantiate or clarify claims; such supporting material enhances the work's authority.
